title: Designing Beyond Language: Sociotechnical Barriers in AI Health Technologies for Limited English Proficiency

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative storyboard-driven semi-structured interviews with patient navigators to evaluate how AI health technologies (like translation tools and chatbots) fail to accommodate regional dialects, colloquialisms, and indigenous languages among Limited English Proficiency (LEP) patients.

Eliciting qualitative feedback using hypothetical storyboard scenarios to identify how Western-centric AI systems might dismiss or misunderstand culturally specific communication styles, traditional health practices (e.g., home remedies, curanderos), and cultural norms surrounding medical authority.

Using storyboard-driven interviews to explore how the design of AI health interventions inherently excludes marginalized populations by assuming baseline levels of digital literacy, reading literacy, and access to modern hardware or stable internet.
